hints.title: Subsequence Frequency Contribution
hints.text: Each element appears in exactly 2^(n-1) possible subsequences.

hints.title: Linearity of Expectation and Sum
hints.text: Distribute summation so each number is weighted by its total occurrences across valid subsets.

hints.title: Modular Exponentiation
hints.text: Compute 2^(n-1) modulo 10^9 + 7 and multiply by the total sum of the array.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def sumOfBeautifulSubsequences(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        # A subsequence is beautiful if adjacent elements differ by at least 1 or satisfy condition
        # Sum of elements across all valid subsequences
        # Precompute contributions: each element x contributes x * 2^(n-1) in all non-empty subsets
        n = len(nums)
        ans = 0
        power = pow(2, n - 1, MOD) if n > 0 else 0
        for x in nums:
            ans = (ans + x * power) % MOD
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Single pass arithmetic leveraging subset contribution symmetry.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Enumerating all 2^N subsets directly takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Evaluates the total in constant auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize element-wise contribution to avoid generating all subsets.
